q: In the Works Programme documents of the Railways, LSWP stands for:

options.A: List of Sanctioned Works Programme
options.B: Lump Sum Works Programme
options.C: List of Selected Works Proposals
options.D: Lump Sum Wages Programme

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The List of Approved Works (LAW), forming Part II of the Pink Book, lists the works sanctioned by the General Manager.
2. Works taken up under the Lump Sum Works Programme (LSWP) are smaller works executed against a lump-sum provision at the zonal and divisional level, instead of being individually itemised in the Pink Book.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Works which are individually listed in the Works Programme, each with its own sanctioned cost and the outlay provided for the year, are known as:

options.A: Itemised works
options.B: Lump-sum works
options.C: Deposit works
options.D: Zonal works

q: The suspense head 'Demands Recoverable' is operated in the railway accounts primarily in order to:

options.A: Record the deposits made by outside bodies for the execution of deposit works
options.B: Watch the liabilities incurred on works but not yet discharged
options.C: Hold the cost of materials lying at the sites of works
options.D: Bring into account, on the accrual basis, dues recoverable by the Railways, such as the rent and lease charges of railway land and buildings and the interest and maintenance charges of private sidings, pending their actual realisation

q: The balance under the suspense head 'Demands Recoverable' is invariably:

options.A: A debit balance, representing dues which have been billed but not yet realised, and shown on the assets side of the Balance Sheet
options.B: A credit balance, representing expenditure incurred but not yet paid for
options.C: A debit balance, representing advances paid to works contractors
options.D: Nil at the close of the financial year, all billed dues being realised within the year itself

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Demands Recoverable is one of the link heads connecting the Government accounts with the Commercial accounts of the Railways.
2. When an amount billed under Demands Recoverable is realised in cash or adjusted, the head is credited, clearing the amount earlier debited to it.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: COFMOW, the centralised agency of the Indian Railways, is primarily responsible for:

options.A: The construction of new railway lines in the North-Eastern region
options.B: The modernisation of railway workshops and production units and the procurement of specialised machinery and plant for them
options.C: The commercial development of vacant railway land
options.D: The execution of railway electrification projects

q: Inspection of the specialised machinery and plant procured centrally by COFMOW is normally carried out by:

options.A: The Railway Board itself
options.B: The contractor supplying the machine
options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General
options.D: RITES

q: Under the General Conditions of Contract for Works, the 'excepted matters', in respect of which the decision of the authority specified in the contract is final and which stand excluded from arbitration, are dealt with in:

options.A: Clause 63
options.B: Clause 64
options.C: Clause 17
options.D: Clause 45

q: Under Clause 64 of the General Conditions of Contract for Works, where the Railway fails to take a decision on the final claim presented by the contractor on disputed matters, the contractor may demand in writing that the dispute or difference be referred to arbitration:

options.A: Immediately on presenting the final claim
options.B: After 30 days, but within 60 days of presenting the final claim
options.C: After 120 days, but within 180 days of presenting the final claim
options.D: Only after the expiry of the defect liability period of the work

q: Under the General Conditions of Contract for Works, the reference to arbitration in a works dispute comprises:

options.A: All disputes between the parties, whether or not any claim has been made in respect of them
options.B: Only the disputes in respect of which a demand for arbitration has been made, with the amounts of claim specified item-wise, together with the counter-claims or set-off given by the Railway
options.C: Only the counter-claims and set-off of the Railway
options.D: All disputes except those relating to the measurement of work

q: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh (RRSK), created to finance safety-related works of the Railways, is in the nature of:

options.A: A lapsable fund, the unspent balance of which lapses at the end of each financial year
options.B: A fund financed entirely out of a cess levied on passenger fares
options.C: A loan account maintained with the Reserve Bank of India
options.D: A non-lapsable fund, the unspent balances of which are carried forward for utilisation on safety works

q: During the evaluation of works tenders, information submitted by a tenderer is found to be false or forged. The consequence under the railway contract conditions is:

options.A: Forfeiture of the tenderer's bid security, besides banning of business dealings with him for a period up to five years
options.B: Only a written warning to the tenderer, his tender being considered on merits
options.C: Rejection of the tender, with no other consequence of any kind
options.D: Levy of liquidated damages on the tenderer

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where information submitted by a tenderer is found to be false or forged after the award of the work, the contract is liable to be terminated and the performance guarantee and security deposit available with the Railways forfeited.
2. Business dealings with such a firm can be banned for a period up to five years.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Where a works requirement can be met only by a particular firm because of its proprietary or specialised nature and a single tender from that firm is proposed, the proprietary nature of the requirement is formally recorded through:

options.A: An urgency certificate issued by the sectional officer
options.B: A Proprietary Article Certificate recorded by the competent authority
options.C: A no-claim certificate furnished by the firm
options.D: A bid security declaration signed by the firm

q: For a consultancy assignment of a highly specialised and complex nature, where the quality of the consultant is of overriding importance, the selection method ordinarily adopted is:

options.A: Least Cost Selection
options.B: Selection based only on the lowest fee quoted
options.C: Nomination of a firm by the executing agency
options.D: Quality Based Selection

q: Under Rule 149 of the General Financial Rules, the procurement through the Government e-Marketplace of goods or services valued above Rs 5 lakh is required to be made by:

options.A: Direct purchase from any seller registered on the portal
options.B: Comparison of the rates of three sellers alone
options.C: Online bidding or reverse auction on the GeM portal
options.D: Open tender outside GeM in all cases

q: Money received by a contractor under the insurance of a work against loss or damage is required, under the conditions of contract, to be:

options.A: Applied solely towards the reinstatement and restoration of the damaged work
options.B: Retained by the contractor as compensation for his loss of profit
options.C: Shared equally between the contractor and the Railways
options.D: Credited to his security deposit account with the Railways

q: Amounts which the Railways are required to pay in satisfaction of a judgment, decree or arbitral award against them are treated in the accounts as:

options.A: Voted expenditure
options.B: Charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: Deposit expenditure
options.D: Suspense expenditure

q: Expenditure of an urgent and unforeseen nature, which cannot await the authorisation of Parliament, may in the first instance be met by an advance from:

options.A: The Depreciation Reserve Fund of the Railways
options.B: The security deposits held from works contractors
options.C: The Railway Safety Fund
options.D: The Contingency Fund of India, the advance being recouped after Parliament authorises the expenditure

q: For a railway establishment, the 'appropriate Government' for the purposes of labour enactments such as the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act and the Minimum Wages Act is:

options.A: The Central Government
options.B: The State Government in whose territory the establishment is situated
options.C: The Railway Board, acting as a State authority
options.D: The local municipal authority of the place

q: A sanction accorded to an item under the Machinery and Plant Programme remains valid, that is, the item may be taken up for procurement under that sanction, for a period of:

options.A: One year
options.B: Two years
options.C: Five years
options.D: Ten years

q: Works relating to the restoration of a dismantled railway line are classified under the Plan Head:

options.A: New Lines
options.B: Restoration of Dismantled Lines
options.C: Gauge Conversion
options.D: Track Renewals

q: Under the Viability Gap Funding scheme of the Government of India, the capital grant provided by the Government of India itself to a public-private partnership project is ordinarily limited to:

options.A: 5 per cent of the total project cost
options.B: 10 per cent of the total project cost
options.C: 40 per cent of the total project cost
options.D: 20 per cent of the total project cost

q: Major railway projects which are beyond the powers of approval of the Ministry of Railways are finally approved, before the investment decision is taken, by:

options.A: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs
options.B: The Public Accounts Committee
options.C: The Railway Convention Committee
options.D: The Comptroller and Auditor General

q: Proposals for major railway projects are appraised, before being placed for investment approval, by the body known as:

options.A: The Works Programme Committee of the Zonal Railway
options.B: The Expanded Board for Railways
options.C: The Tender Committee of the Railway Board
options.D: The Finance Commission

q: 'Demands Payable', the link head operated on the expenditure side of the railway accounts, ordinarily shows:

options.A: A debit balance, representing earnings billed but not yet realised
options.B: A debit balance, representing advances paid to works contractors
options.C: A credit balance, representing expenditure which has been incurred and brought to account but has not yet been paid for
options.D: A credit balance, representing the deposits made by outside bodies for deposit works

q: As distinct from the test check exercised by statutory audit, the internal check of contractors' bills in the railway Accounts office is exercised:

options.A: On a sample of ten per cent of the bills passed
options.B: Only on bills exceeding a prescribed value
options.C: Only on the final bills of contracts
options.D: On all the bills, that is, on a cent per cent basis

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, the wage period fixed for the payment of wages to the workmen engaged on a work shall not exceed:

options.A: One month
options.B: Two months
options.C: One quarter
options.D: Six months

q: A tender submitted on behalf of a partnership firm, a company or a joint venture is required to be accompanied by:

options.A: The income-tax returns of all the partners or directors for the last three years
options.B: Attested copies of the constitution documents of the firm or company and of its Permanent Account Number (PAN) card
options.C: A solvency certificate from a nationalised bank in all cases
options.D: Completion certificates of all the works executed by the firm since its formation

q: In a works contract, the amount of work done against the material component in a bill is Rs 10,00,000. The Wholesale Price Index for the material rises from 200 in the base period to 210 for the period of the bill. The price variation payable on the material component is:

In a tender for a work, the amount arrived at by multiplying the unit rate quoted for an item with the quantity of the item differs from the total amount written by the tenderer against that item. In evaluating the tender, the discrepancy is ordinarily resolved by treating as correct:

options.A: The total amount written by the tenderer
options.B: The higher of the two amounts
options.C: The average of the two amounts
options.D: The amount arrived at from the quoted unit rate, the unit rate prevailing over the extended total

q: Where a tenderer has quoted a rate for an item both in figures and in words and the two do not agree, the rate ordinarily taken as the rate quoted by him is:

options.A: The rate in words
options.B: The rate in figures
options.C: The lower of the two rates
options.D: The higher of the two rates

q: A work such as yard remodelling comprises portions to be executed by the Engineering, Signalling and Electrical departments. For the sanction of such a work:

options.A: Each department sanctions a separate independent estimate and no combined document is prepared
options.B: The portion of the estimate pertaining to each department is prepared by that department and the portions are combined into a single composite estimate for sanction
options.C: Only the Engineering portion is estimated, the remaining portions being executed without any estimate
options.D: The work is sanctioned on a lump-sum oral assessment made by the Divisional Railway Manager

q: The cess collected under the Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Cess Act from the bills of works contractors is remitted to:

options.A: The Consolidated Fund of India, as a receipt of tax revenue
options.B: The Depreciation Reserve Fund of the Railways
options.C: The State Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Board
options.D: The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation

q: A receipt given in acknowledgement of money paid by the Railways, where the amount received exceeds Rs 5,000, is required under the Indian Stamp Act to bear:

options.A: A court fee stamp
options.B: No stamp of any kind
options.C: The signature of two gazetted officers
options.D: A revenue stamp

q: Under the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act and the rules made under it, a contractor engaging contract labour on a railway work is required to issue to every workman engaged by him:

options.A: An employment card and wage slips, so that his engagement and the wages paid to him remain on record
options.B: A railway privilege pass for travel to the site of work
options.C: A certificate of partnership in the contractor's firm
options.D: A completion certificate at the end of every month

q: Under the General Financial Rules, the earnest money (bid security) of the unsuccessful bidders for a work is required to be refunded:

options.A: Only after the work has been completed and its final bill paid
options.B: At the earliest after the expiry of the bid validity, and in any case not later than 30 days after the award of the contract
options.C: After one year from the date of opening of the tenders
options.D: Only on a specific written demand made by each unsuccessful bidder

q: Vacant railway land entrusted to the Rail Development Authority for commercial development is ordinarily given out on lease for a period extending up to:

options.A: 10 years
options.B: 30 years
options.C: 99 years
options.D: 999 years

q: Under Clause 64 of the General Conditions of Contract for Works, the bar contained in sub-section (5) of Section 12 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 on the appointment of certain persons as arbitrator:

options.A: Can never be relaxed between the parties to the contract
options.B: Stands waived automatically on the signing of the agreement
options.C: Applies only to the contractor and not to the Railways
options.D: May be waived by the parties by an express agreement in writing made after the dispute has arisen

q: The redevelopment of major railway stations is planned to be financed substantially through:

options.A: Commercial development of the land and air space at and around the stations
options.B: A special cess on passenger fares earmarked for each station
options.C: Loans raised personally by the station managers
options.D: Outright sale of the stations to private parties

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Rolling Stock Programme covers the acquisition of locomotives, coaches and wagons for the Railways.
2. The Machinery and Plant Programme covers the provision of machinery and plant for workshops, running sheds and other units.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Works Register, in which the expenditure on each work is watched against its sanctioned estimate, is maintained by the executive office.
2. The Register of Sanctions, in which the sanctions accorded to estimates and to expenditure are recorded for the purpose of internal check, is maintained in the Accounts office.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Funds may be re-appropriated from a work charged to Capital to a work charged to Revenue with the sanction of the General Manager.
2. Re-appropriation cannot be made to meet expenditure on a 'New Service' which has not been brought to the notice of Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Under the General Conditions of Contract for Works, the arbitral proceedings in a works dispute are treated as having commenced from:

options.A: The date of issue of the Letter of Acceptance of the work
options.B: The date on which the contractor first raised his claim orally at the site
options.C: The date of appointment of the arbitral tribunal
options.D: The day on which a written and valid demand for arbitration is received by the Railway

q: 'Way-leave charges' recovered by the Railways from a public body or a private party represent:

options.A: The rent of railway land leased out for a shop or godown
options.B: A licence fee for running a catering stall at a station
options.C: A fee charged for permitting the party's pipes, cables, drains or similar works to pass through or across railway land
options.D: A penalty imposed for encroachment on railway land

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A licence of railway land merely permits the licensee to use the land for the stated purpose and creates no interest or estate in the land itself.
2. A lease of railway land, unlike a licence, conveys an interest in the land to the lessee for the term of the lease.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The 'social service obligations' borne by the Indian Railways refer to:

options.A: The expenditure incurred on the staff benefit fund and railway schools
options.B: The losses accepted on uneconomic services and concessional or below-cost carriage undertaken in the wider public and social interest
options.C: The dividend payable by the Railways to the General Revenues
options.D: The contribution made by the Railways to the pension fund of its employees

q: In railway working, transactions between one railway administration and another, and with other Government departments, that are settled through book adjustment without cash payment are broadly described as:

options.A: Deposit transactions
options.B: Suspense transactions
options.C: Remittance transactions
options.D: Book adjustment (transfer) transactions

q: The Indian Railway Conference Association (IRCA) is principally associated with:

options.A: The framing of rules and procedures for the interchange of traffic, including coaching and goods tariff matters, among the railways
options.B: The sanction of works estimates of the zonal railways
options.C: The audit of railway accounts on behalf of the C&AG
options.D: The procurement of stores for all zonal railways

q: A loss of stores or cash in a railway office is 'written off' the accounts when:

options.A: The amount is transferred to a suspense head pending recovery
options.B: The amount is adjusted as a savings against another head of account
options.C: The amount is recovered in instalments from the pay of the official at fault
options.D: The competent authority sanctions the removal of the irrecoverable amount from the books, after the prescribed enquiries

q: As distinct from a 'write-off', a 'write-back' in works accounts denotes:

options.A: Sanctioning the removal of an irrecoverable loss from the books
options.B: Recovering an amount from the contractor's security deposit
options.C: Writing a fresh estimate in place of a lapsed estimate
options.D: Restoring to the proper head an amount earlier charged or credited in error or in anticipation, by a correcting adjustment

q: Under the conditions of a works contract, subletting or assignment of the contract by the contractor is:

options.A: Freely permitted, the Railway having no concern with it
options.B: Permitted only for contracts below a prescribed value
options.C: Not permitted without the prior written consent of the Railway; unauthorised subletting can lead to termination of the contract
options.D: Permitted provided the sub-contractor is registered with the Railways

q: A 'virtual completion certificate' in connection with a work is issued to record that:

options.A: The work is substantially complete and fit for the purpose for which it was intended, so that the maintenance period and allied time limits can run from that date
options.B: The estimate of the work has been administratively approved
options.C: The final bill of the contractor has been passed for payment
options.D: The work has been inspected by the Finance branch before sanction

q: At the time a completed work is taken over, the list of minor defects and items still requiring attention, which the contractor must rectify, is commonly recorded as:

options.A: The liability statement
options.B: The snag (punch) list
options.C: The deviation statement
options.D: The hindrance statement

q: Where a contractor fails to pay wages to the labour engaged by him on a railway work, the Railways, as principal employer, may:

options.A: Refuse to take over the completed work in every case
options.B: Blacklist the labourers concerned
options.C: Debar the zonal railway from engaging contract labour
options.D: Disburse the unpaid wages to the labour through the Railway and recover the amount so paid from the dues of the contractor

q: For labour employed departmentally on a work, the daily record of the labour engaged and the wages payable to each person is maintained in the:

options.A: Measurement book
options.B: Muster roll
options.C: Contractor's ledger
options.D: Materials-at-site register

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A contractor executing a railway work is required to comply with the Employees' Provident Fund provisions in respect of the labour engaged by him.
2. Where the contractor defaults in depositing the provident fund contributions of his labour, the amount can be recovered from his dues as the liability of the principal employer.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

q: A 'mobilisation advance' in a works contract is an advance paid to the contractor:

options.A: After the completion of the work, along with the final bill
options.B: Towards the cost of materials brought to the site of the work
options.C: At the commencement of the work, to enable him to mobilise labour, plant and resources for starting the work, recoverable from his running bills
options.D: In lieu of the security deposit required under the contract

q: A 'plant and machinery advance' under a works contract differs from a secured advance in that it is granted:

options.A: Against the security of materials brought to the site and not yet incorporated in the work
options.B: Only after the final bill of the work has been measured
options.C: Against the plant and machinery brought to the site by the contractor for use on the work, subject to the conditions of the contract
options.D: Without any recovery being made from the running bills of the contractor

q: In the analysis of a rate for an earthwork item, 'lead' refers to:

options.A: The vertical height through which the excavated earth is lifted
options.B: The horizontal distance over which the excavated earth is carried and deposited
options.C: The depth of excavation below the ground level
options.D: The extra width provided at the formation level

q: In the analysis of a rate for an earthwork item, 'lift' refers to:

options.A: The vertical height through which the excavated earth is raised for disposal
options.B: The horizontal distance over which the earth is transported
options.C: The slope given to the sides of a cutting
options.D: The thickness of a layer of earth filling

q: An item of work not provided for in the sanctioned schedule or estimate, which becomes necessary during execution and for which no similar scheduled rate exists, is ordinarily paid for at a rate derived from the market and known as:

options.A: A reduced rate
options.B: A penal rate
options.C: A star (market) rate
options.D: A departmental rate

q: A 'temporary imprest' held by an engineering official, as distinct from a permanent imprest, is:

options.A: A fixed advance recouped as and when it is spent, without any time limit
options.B: An advance given for a specific work or occasion, which must be accounted for and closed and is not recouped as a standing advance
options.C: An advance which the official may retain as his personal pay
options.D: An advance given only to gazetted officers for travelling expenses

q: The suspense head 'Miscellaneous Works Advances' in the works accounts principally accommodates:

options.A: The deposits received from outside bodies for deposit works
options.B: The wages of labour remaining unpaid at the end of the month
options.C: The value of stores issued to works but not yet adjusted
options.D: Advances paid in connection with works, such as advances to contractors, which remain recoverable or adjustable against the works concerned

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A reconnaissance survey of a proposed new line is a rapid preliminary examination of the country to select the possible alignments worth detailed investigation.
2. A final location survey is carried out on the alignment finally selected, with detailed pegging and levelling, on the basis of which the detailed estimate and construction plans are prepared.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The purpose of a Preliminary Engineering-cum-Traffic Survey (PETS) for a proposed railway line is to:

options.A: Assess the feasibility of the proposal, covering both the engineering features of the possible alignments and the traffic expected to be carried, before an investment decision is taken
options.B: Fix the final alignment and peg out the centre line on the ground
options.C: Prepare the working drawings for bridges on the selected alignment
options.D: Carry out the land acquisition proceedings for the project

q: A 'hindrance register' maintained at the site of a work serves to record:

options.A: The daily attendance of the departmental labour on the work
options.B: The defects noticed in the completed portions of the work
options.C: The hindrances and interruptions affecting the progress of the work, with their dates and causes, which become material when extension of time or delay claims are considered
options.D: The materials received at the site from the stores depots

q: 'Foreclosure' of a works contract, as distinct from its termination for the contractor's default, takes place when:

options.A: The contractor abandons the work without notice
options.B: The contract is closed by the Railway because the work itself is abandoned or curtailed for reasons not attributable to the contractor's default
options.C: The contractor assigns the contract to another firm
options.D: The period of the contract expires by efflux of time

q: On completion of a work executed under a construction or project organisation, the asset created is brought on to the books of the open-line (revenue) organisation through:

options.A: A fresh sanction of the Railway Board in every case
options.B: The completion report and the transfer of the asset, with its cost, to the open-line accounts and asset registers
options.C: A sale of the asset to the open-line organisation
options.D: Writing off the cost of the asset against the Depreciation Reserve Fund

q: The normal effect of a 'force majeure' event under a works contract is that:

options.A: Neither party is held liable for the failure to perform the obligations prevented by the event, and time and allied relief are dealt with as provided in the contract
options.B: The contractor becomes entitled to payment for the work not executed
options.C: The security deposit of the contractor is forfeited automatically
options.D: The contract stands converted into a cost-plus contract

q: Departmental materials issued to a contractor for use on a work are ordinarily:

options.A: Given free of cost and never adjusted in his bills
options.B: Charged to him at the issue rate, the value being recovered by deduction from his bills as the materials are consumed on the work
options.C: Sold outright to him at the market rate on the day of issue
options.D: Recorded only in the site order book, with no accountal anywhere

q: 'Test check' of the measurements recorded for a work by the recording official is exercised in order to:

options.A: Dispense with the recording of measurements altogether
options.B: Transfer the contractor's ledger to the Accounts office
options.C: Verify, by an independent check of a portion of the measurements by a superior or other authorised official, that the recorded measurements are correct
options.D: Authorise payment of the contractor's bill without measurement

q: In the abstract of the cost of an estimate for a work, the provision made under 'contingencies' is intended to cover:

options.A: The cost of land required for the work
options.B: The pay of the regular establishment supervising the work
options.C: The interest charges on the capital invested in the work
options.D: Petty and unforeseen items of expenditure incidental to the work which cannot be foreseen or detailed at the estimate stage

q: Staff whose pay and allowances are charged directly to the estimate of a work, for the period they are employed on that work, are described as:

options.A: Work-charged establishment
options.B: Permanent establishment
options.C: Supernumerary establishment
options.D: Ex-cadre establishment

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Concurrence' of Finance is the formal agreement of the Finance branch to a proposal involving expenditure, signifying that it is financially in order.
2. 'Vetting' by Finance is the examination and checking of a document such as an estimate, a tender schedule or a contractor's bill calculation for its arithmetical and financial correctness.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

q: In connection with the execution of a work, 'completion drawings' are:

options.A: The drawings issued to the tenderers along with the tender documents
options.B: Drawings prepared on completion showing the work exactly as it has actually been executed, incorporating all deviations from the original drawings
options.C: The sketches attached to the abstract estimate of the work
options.D: The survey drawings prepared before the work is sanctioned

q: A tenderer who has submitted his tender subsequently seeks to withdraw it within the validity period of the tender. The ordinary consequence under the tender conditions is:

options.A: Nothing; a tender may be withdrawn at any time without consequence
options.B: The tender is kept pending for the next work of the Railway
options.C: The contractor is debarred from all future railway works permanently
options.D: Forfeiture of his earnest money, in accordance with the conditions of tender

q: In a works contract based on a schedule of items and quantities, payment to the contractor for an item is ordinarily made:

options.A: For the quantity of the item actually executed and measured, at the rate accepted for that item
options.B: For the full quantity shown in the schedule, whether executed or not
options.C: On a lump sum for all items together, without item-wise measurement
options.D: Only after the whole work is completed, in a single payment

q: The 'Letter of Acceptance' issued to the successful tenderer of a work signifies that:

options.A: The work has been physically completed and taken over
options.B: The final bill of the work has been admitted in audit
options.C: His tender has been accepted, whereupon a binding contract comes into existence between the Railway and the contractor on the terms of the tender documents
options.D: The earnest money deposited by him has been refunded

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. On the issue of the Letter of Acceptance, the earnest money of the successful tenderer is adjusted towards the security deposit of the work.
2. The earnest money of the unsuccessful tenderers is refundable to them after the tender is decided.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 2 only
options.C: 1 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A contractor executing a work near a running line must observe the safety precautions prescribed for working near running trains because:

options.A: The Railway's liability for accidents during such working is governed by the conditions of the contract and the safety rules, and unauthorised interference with running lines can endanger train safety
options.B: Such precautions apply only to works executed departmentally
options.C: The contractor is treated as a railway servant for all purposes
options.D: No trains are permitted to run while any work is in progress anywhere on the section

q: Where land is required for a sanctioned railway work, the compensation payable to the landowners is, in accountal terms:

options.A: Charged to the revenue account of the Railway in all cases
options.B: Borne by the contractor executing the work
options.C: Debited to the estimate of the work as part of the cost of land, on the basis of the award and the payment made through the land acquisition machinery
options.D: Met from the security deposits of works contractors

q: A works contract provides that the completion period shall be reckoned from the date of issue of the Letter of Acceptance. The significance of reckoning the period in this manner is that:

options.A: Liquidated damages and extension of time are both judged against the completion date so arrived at
options.B: The contractor may start the work at any time within five years
options.C: The security deposit need not be deposited at all
options.D: The measurements of the work need not be recorded

q: In tender evaluation, a tender in which essential information such as rates against items is left blank or the tender is qualified by the tenderer's own conditions contrary to the tender documents is liable to be treated as:

options.A: The lowest tender in all cases
options.B: A responsive tender entitled to preference
options.C: A post-tender offer
options.D: A non-responsive (invalid) tender and rejected

q: The charges levied on a work towards the cost of the tools and plant of the department used on the work are distinct from the general establishment charges in that they represent:

options.A: The dividend payable on the capital cost of the work
options.B: A percentage provision for the use, wear and maintenance of the departmental tools and plant employed on the work
options.C: The cost of land acquired for the work
options.D: The interest accrued during the construction period

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Expenditure on a work must be booked under the allocation and plan head prescribed for it, irrespective of whether budget provision exists under that head.
2. The absence of budget provision does not by itself alter the correct classification of the expenditure on a work.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

q: Where a work, on completion, is found to have been executed at a cost less than its sanctioned estimate and no further expenditure is to be incurred on it, the correct course is to:

options.A: Keep the estimate open indefinitely so that the savings can be used on other works
options.B: Close the work through a completion report, surrendering the savings against the sanctioned estimate
options.C: Transfer the savings to the security deposits of the contractor
options.D: Book the savings as miscellaneous earnings of the Railway

q: A 'letter of credit' arrangement sometimes stipulated in a supply or works arrangement operates as:

options.A: A written undertaking by a bank, at the instance of the buyer, to honour payment to the supplier on presentation of the stipulated documents
options.B: A letter from the Railway authorising the contractor to start the work
options.C: A credit note issued by the Accounts office to the contractor
options.D: Permission to the contractor to sublet a part of the contract

q: The record of the daily progress of a work, the labour and plant deployed and the events at the site is maintained at the site in the:

options.A: Contractor's ledger
options.B: Site order book / daily work diary maintained by the official in charge of the work
options.C: Register of sanctions maintained in the Accounts office
options.D: Tender register maintained in the headquarters office

q: 'Determination' of a works contract by the Railway, as distinct from its foreclosure, takes place when:

options.A: The work itself is abandoned by the Railway for reasons unconnected with the contractor
options.B: The Railway puts an end to the contract on account of the contractor's defaults or breaches specified in the contract, after following the notice procedure prescribed therein
options.C: The contract period simply expires and a fresh tender is invited
options.D: The contractor completes the work and submits his final bill

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The several documents forming a works contract are to be read together as mutually explanatory of one another.
2. Where a conflict between two contract documents cannot be so reconciled, it is resolved in accordance with the order of precedence laid down in the contract.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Measurements of a work recorded jointly by the Railway's representative and the contractor or his authorised representative, and signed by both at the site, are resorted to principally in order to:

options.A: Avoid subsequent disputes about the quantities executed, since both parties have participated in and accepted the recording
options.B: Dispense with the maintenance of the measurement book altogether
options.C: Fix the rates payable for items not covered by the contract
options.D: Transfer the liability for defective work from the contractor to the Railway

q: A check of the 'theoretical consumption' of a departmentally supplied material such as cement or steel on a work serves to:

options.A: Fix the market rate at which the material is to be recovered from the contractor
options.B: Decide the quantity of the material to be ordered for the next work
options.C: Certify the structural strength of the completed work
options.D: Compare the quantity that ought to have been consumed, as worked out from the drawings and the measured work, with the quantity actually consumed, so that excess consumption is explained or recovered

q: A tender signed and submitted not by the tenderer himself but by another person on his behalf must be supported by:

options.A: A completion certificate of an earlier work executed by the tenderer
options.B: A solvency certificate issued by the tenderer's bankers
options.C: A power of attorney or other proper authority showing that the signatory is duly authorised to sign and bind the tenderer
options.D: A no-claim certificate from the tenderer's previous employer

q: As a step towards resolving a contract dispute without arbitration, 'conciliation' differs from arbitration principally in that:

options.A: The conciliator passes a binding award which can be executed like a decree
options.B: The conciliator only assists and persuades the parties to arrive at an amicable settlement themselves and does not himself adjudicate the dispute
options.C: Conciliation can be resorted to only after an arbitral award has been set aside by a court
options.D: Conciliation is conducted by the tender committee of the Railway

q: A labourer engaged by a works contractor is injured in an accident arising out of and in the course of his employment on the work, and the contractor fails to pay the compensation payable under the Employees' Compensation Act. In such a case:

options.A: No compensation is payable to anyone, the man being the contractor's employee
options.B: The compensation can be paid only out of the labourer's own provident fund
options.C: The injured labourer must recover the amount from the Railway Board directly
options.D: The Railway, as principal employer, may have to pay the compensation and can recover the amount so paid from the contractor's dues

q: During the evaluation of tenders for a work, the tenders received show identical unusual rates, a pattern of rotation of the lowest bids among the same few firms and other signs of an understanding among the tenderers. Such bidding is treated as:

options.A: Collusive bidding, rendering the tenders liable to rejection and the firms liable to action under the tender conditions
options.B: A healthy competition to be encouraged by accepting the lowest tender
options.C: A matter to be ignored once the lowest rate is otherwise reasonable
options.D: Grounds for raising the estimated cost of the work

q: Where the bid of the lowest tenderer for a work is found to be seriously unbalanced or abnormally low in relation to the estimated cost, so that its acceptance carries a performance risk, the Railway may protect its interest by:

options.A: Accepting the bid without any safeguard, the low rate itself being sufficient protection
options.B: Rejecting all the tenders and abandoning the work in every such case
options.C: Requiring the successful bidder to furnish an additional performance security, in accordance with the tender conditions, before the work is awarded
options.D: Directing the bidder to raise his rates to the level of the second lowest tenderer

q: The decision on a tender could not be finalised before the validity period of the tenders expired. The correct course in such a situation is to:

options.A: Treat all the tenders as automatically valid for one more year
options.B: Seek, before the expiry of the validity period, the written consent of the tenderers to extend the validity, the earnest money remaining valid for the extended period
options.C: Open fresh tenders without informing the earlier tenderers at all
options.D: Accept the lowest tender after expiry without any extension, the delay being on the Railway's side
